messages:
emma: FYI customer ACME reported a big p95/p99 latency regression starting ~08:40UTC, they see ~10s+ tails and a ton of "pending_requests" in our dashboard. they included a request_id: req_9f2c7b.
kai: thanks — can you paste the most recent logs / the ingress admission lines for that request_id? also tenant/org id so we can scope.
emma: org=acme-inc, req=req_9f2c7b. logs: ```2026-03-16T08:40:12Z ingress svc=api admission=queued tenant=acme-inc pending_requests=312
2026-03-16T08:40:12Z worker-pool warn=worker-saturated replicas=8 inflight=256 queue_depth=312
2026-03-16T08:40:13Z ingress error=admission_rejected reason=concurrency_limit tenant=acme-inc``` customer says retries just pile up.
priya: oncall here — looks like admission control hit hard. metric spike for pending_requests and inflight. Any recent deploys to the routing/admission service in the last hour?
kai: no user-facing deploys in the last hour from runtime. saw an infra greenlet change earlier but not related. I'm checking admission config: default max_concurrency=32 per-worker, per-tenant burstpad disabled for acme.
matt: throttling/fairness maybe mis-evaluating tenant weight; I see we recently tightened soft_deadline from 200ms->150ms in the last rollout (03:20 UTC). That can reduce throughput for long-running requests and cause queue pileup. Could be regression.
emma: customer says they were using streaming on large prompts, so individual token streams are slower. they hit p95 spikes after that config change? timeline fits.
kai: mitigation suggestion: 1) temporarily increase worker replicas for the affected deployment 2) relax soft_deadline / admission threshold for acme 3) enable tenant burstpad for their org. who can do the quick change?
priya: I can lift replicas and toggle a policy on the control plane. I'll do a safe +50% replica bump and enable burstpad for acme for 15m. pushing now.
deploy-bot: release-controller: scale request accepted for service=ingress-runtime replicas: 8 -> 12 (start)
deploy-bot: release-controller: policy update applied: tenant=acme-inc burstpad=enabled ttl=15m
matt: also rolling a tiny hotfix to the admission evaluator to fallback to a cheaper model variant earlier (so long prompts get routed to quantized variant automatically if latency SLOs are threatened). i'll push canary to 1 pod.
kai: good. meanwhile to reduce customer retries, support can advise acme to add header `x-request-priority: low` for non-urgent batch calls so they queue differently.
emma: messaged customer with the mitigations and asked them to hold off retries for 10m. also provided a curl repro they sent: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"g-large","input":"<2000-token>","stream":true}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate``` asked for sample response times and request_id if it happens again.
priya: scaling finished. replicas reported 12 healthy. burstpad enabled. monitoring now — pending_requests for acme dropped from 312 -> 48 over 3 mins.
matt: canary for admission fallback rolled; I'll watch p95s for the next 10m. also started a flamegraph perf capture for a representative worker and saved to /var/tmp/ingress-perf-1818889999.
kai: recorded action items: 1) revert soft_deadline tightening and run benchmark across long streaming requests (owner: eng-runtime/matt) 2) add automated canary for admission parameter rollouts (owner: eng-sre/kai) 3) document tenant burstpad policy for support runbooks (owner: support/emma).
emma: customer updated: they confirm latency improved and retries subsided. asked for postmortem and timeline. closing loop with them in 24h.
priya: marking incident mitigated. leaving monitor alert at reduced threshold for 2 hours. i'll create follow-up ticket for config rollback testing.
emma: thanks all :thumbsup:
